close_reason: added check_critical_extensions with handled OID set; all unknown critical exts rejected
description:
Implement check_critical_extensions(cert: &Certificate, is_ca: bool) -> Result<()> that rejects any critical extension whose OID is not in the handled set.

RFC 5280 §6.1.3(a)(3): if a critical extension is not recognized or not processed, path validation must fail.

Handled critical extension OIDs for v0.1 (these are processed by the §6.1 state machine):
  2.5.29.15 — KeyUsage
  2.5.29.19 — BasicConstraints
  2.5.29.17 — SubjectAltName (recognized but not validated by pkix-path; validation is application responsibility)

Unhandled if critical (must reject):
  2.5.29.30 — NameConstraints  (v0.2 feature; for now, critical NameConstraints = error)
  2.5.29.32 — CertificatePolicies (v0.2)
  2.5.29.36 — PolicyConstraints (v0.2)
  2.5.29.54 — InhibitAnyPolicy (v0.2)
  Any other OID not in the handled list

Non-critical extensions: always ignored (even if unrecognized). RFC 5280 §4.2 explicitly permits this.

Returns Error::UnhandledCriticalExtension { index } on failure (index injected by caller).

Note: SubjectKeyIdentifier (2.5.29.14) and AuthorityKeyIdentifier (2.5.29.35) MUST NOT be marked critical per RFC 5280 §4.2.1.1–2; if they are, they fall through to the unhandled check and cause an error. That is correct behavior.
title: pkix-path: critical extension guard
